decision.hypothesis: Inherited model misclassifies development cracks as warping. Amplifying 64 channels with the strongest positive crack-versus-warp activation contrast may preserve crack evidence through the last blocks. This is a small diagnostic perturbation, chosen after reading the inherited confusion matrices.

observed: probe-01/feedback.json: 90/100 development, 29/40 selection, crack correct unchanged; reject probe 01

decision.hypothesis: Probe 01 moved a crack error from warping to layer shift without fixing it. Rather than amplify existing channels, add a development-derived crack correction at block 9, before inherited block 10. Fit zero desired change for other development cases; use stronger regularization than the prior grid to reduce memorization.

observed: probe-02/feedback.json: unchanged confusion, patch norm 0.01035; insufficient intervention size remains plausible

decision.hypothesis: Probe 02 changed no decisions and had weight-delta norm 0.01035. Test the same direction at norm about 0.414, still below the inherited edit norm 1.132, to distinguish insufficient amplitude from a useless direction. Chosen after probe 02 feedback, not a predeclared sweep.

observed: probe-03/feedback.json: cracks 4 to 7 on selection, layer shifts 9 to 5; total 29 to 28. Reject broad class correction and add development-class protection.

decision.hypothesis: Probe 03 fixed 3 selection cracks but made 4 layer-shift samples false cracks. Keep the crack correction direction while fitting a counter-direction on development layer-shift samples to reduce their crack logit. Use only development labels to fit; same block and strength isolate this protection change.

observed: probe-04/feedback.json: selection 25/40, patch norm 1.476; protection overwhelms desired correction

decision.hypothesis: Probe 04 protection dominated: patch norm increased from 0.414 to 1.476 and crack selection fell to 2/10. Reduce only protection by 10x while preserving the useful crack direction. This tests whether mild class-specific protection can recover the layer-shift regressions without erasing crack evidence.

observed: probe-05/feedback.json: 95/100 development but 25/40 selection; abandon crack-only correction and asymmetric protection

decision.hypothesis: Both strong and weak crack-only protection failed to improve held-out selection. Abandon the one-class hypothesis: fit a simultaneous residual correction for all remaining development mistakes so layer-shift errors receive their own positive correction. Use block 9 before inherited block 10, moderate gain, and the previously useful ridge fraction.

observed: probe-06/feedback.json: 100/100 development, 28/40 selection; reduce amplitude rather than pursue training fit

decision.hypothesis: Probe 06 achieved perfect development classification but selection dropped to 28/40: over-adaptation. Reduce only intervention amplitude to 30%, producing expected norm about 0.384, to test a conservative version. If it cannot improve selection, reject this branch and retain the inherited checkpoint.

decision.reason: Agent selects probe 07 after feedback: only tested candidate with selection accuracy above inherited 29/40 (30/40). One-example gain is weak; freeze now, do not continue tuning on selection or test.

decision: reject probe-07 after final evaluation; retain inherited checkpoint
reason: Final new-frame test decreased from 29/60 to 27/60 despite selection gain. No post-test tuning.
